questions.question: Explain the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE. Why is PKCE required for SPAs?
questions.title: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE — SPA Auth Flow
questions.direct_answer:
Explain the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE. Why is PKCE required for SPAs?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser, network, and server contract (headers, cookies, streams)), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Code flow: auth request → code → token exchange; PKCE adds code_verifier/code_challenge to prevent code-interception attacks for public clients.

**Classic weak answer:** Using the implicit flow for SPAs in 2026 — deprecated; Auth Code + PKCE is the recommended flow.

**Senior finish:** Walk through each step; note auth0, Okta, Keycloak all default to PKCE for SPAs now.

interviewer_intent.testing: Code flow: auth request → code → token exchange; PKCE adds code_verifier/code_challenge to prevent code-interception attacks for public clients
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using the implicit flow for SPAs in 2026 — deprecated; Auth Code + PKCE is the recommended flow
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Walk through each step; note auth0, Okta, Keycloak all default to PKCE for SPAs now

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE — SPA Auth Flow** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** Explain the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE. Why is PKCE required for SPAs?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Code flow: auth request → code → token exchange; PKCE adds code_verifier/code_challenge to prevent code-interception attacks for public clients**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Using the implicit flow for SPAs in 2026 — deprecated; Auth Code + PKCE is the recommended flow**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Walk through each step; note auth0, Okta, Keycloak all default to PKCE for SPAs now**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Code flow: auth request → code → token exchange; PKCE adds code_verifier/code_challenge to prevent code-interception attacks for public clients
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Mental model (flowchart)
sections.content:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant U as Browser (SPA)
    participant I as Identity Provider
    participant B as BFF / API
    participant R as Resource API
    U->>I: Authorize (PKCE / code)
    I-->>U: Authorization code
    U->>B: Exchange code (server-side)
    B->>I: Token endpoint + client auth
    I-->>B: Access + refresh (optional)
    B-->>U: HttpOnly session cookie
    U->>R: API call (credentials include)
    Note over U,R: Tokens never in localStorage when using BFF pattern
```

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **using the implicit flow for SPAs in 2026 — deprecated; Auth Code + PKCE is the recommended flow** and what you do instead.

questions.question: Why is the OAuth 2.0 Implicit flow deprecated?
questions.title: Why the OAuth 2.0 Implicit Flow Is Deprecated (2026)
questions.direct_answer:
Why is the OAuth 2.0 Implicit flow deprecated?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser, network, and server contract (headers, cookies, streams)), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Access tokens in URL fragments (leakable, not confidential); no client secret; PKCE + code flow is the secure replacement.

**Classic weak answer:** Still defending Implicit as 'simpler' — security community (RFC 9700) explicitly recommends against it since 2019.

**Senior finish:** Reference OAuth 2.1 (draft) which removes Implicit entirely and mandates PKCE.

interviewer_intent.testing: Access tokens in URL fragments (leakable, not confidential); no client secret; PKCE + code flow is the secure replacement
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Still defending Implicit as 'simpler' — security community (RFC 9700) explicitly recommends against it since 2019
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Reference OAuth 2.1 (draft) which removes Implicit entirely and mandates PKCE
